prompt:
What is the time complexity of this code, where n is a positive whole number (the input size)? Assume constant-cost calls to work() and loop arithmetic.

```python
i = 1
while i < n:
    # Inner lengths: 1, 2, 4, 8, ...
    for j in range(i):
        work()
    i *= 2
```

options.explanation: Correct. The inner loop runs 1 + 2 + 4 + ... times, up to the last power of 2 below n. That geometric series sums to less than 2 × n, so the total is Θ(n). Here n is the input item count.

This charges the largest inner count on every outer iteration, but most outer iterations have much shorter inner loops. Sum the actual inner lengths instead of multiplying the largest length by the number of outer calls.
This counts only the outer loop. Each outer pass also runs i calls to work(), and i gets large.
No inner pass exceeds the input bound, and there are only logarithmically many outer passes. A quadratic total is far too high.

workedExample: The inner lengths double from one until just below the bound. All earlier lengths add up to less than twice the last one. The last length is itself a constant fraction of n, so matching linear upper and lower bounds give Θ(n). Multiplying every outer pass by the largest inner length charges work that never happened.

